# Model and source

```{r meta}
mod <- readModelDb("Kato_2017_amikacin")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
mod_meta <- mod_ui$meta
```

* Citation: `r mod_meta$reference`
* Description: `r mod_meta$description`
* Article (DOI): <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40268-016-0165-5>

Kato 2017 describes amikacin in 35 hospitalized Japanese adults with a
two-compartment model fitted in Phoenix NLME (WinNonlin 6.3). Clearance is
directly proportional to Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance (CCr) and the
central volume is directly proportional to body weight. The paper then
simulates the concentration 1 h after the start of a 30 min infusion (Cpeak)
for 10-30 mg/kg single doses and reports the probability of attaining
Cpeak/MIC >= 8 (Figure 2) and of a trough below 4 mg/L (Results text). This
vignette checks the packaged model against those simulation results.

# Population

The analysis is a single-centre retrospective therapeutic drug monitoring study
at Aichi Medical University Hospital, Japan (September 2009 - December 2014).
Thirty-five of 39 eligible patients were included (four lacked infusion-time
records), 25 male and 10 female, aged 15-95 years (median 70). They were light
(median weight 49.5 kg, range 32.5-78; mean BMI 19.6) and hypoalbuminaemic
(mean albumin 2.7 g/dL). Median Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance was 60.0
mL/min (range 6.1-144). Infections were bacteremia, pneumonia and urinary tract
infection, and *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* was the commonest isolate. Amikacin was
given once daily at 200-1000 mg (median 9.6 mg/kg) by 0.5 h or 1 h infusion,
and 65 serum concentrations (1-2 per patient, a trough and/or a peak 1 h after
the start of infusion) were measured (Kato 2017 Table 1, Patients and Data
Collection). Patients on continuous renal replacement therapy were excluded.

```{r population}
str(mod_meta$population)
```

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: two compartments, first-order elimination, IV infusion | -- | Population PK Parameters of Amikacin ('the two-compartment model better described the current data set') |
| `lcl` (theta1, CL at CCr = 60.0 mL/min) | log(2.41) L/h | Table 4, theta1 = 2.41 |
| `lvc` (theta2, V1 at weight = 49.5 kg) | log(10.70) L | Table 4, theta2 = 10.70 |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(7.72) L | Table 4 footnote, 'V2 (L) = 7.72' |
| `lq` (Q) | log(7.0) L/h | Table 4 footnote, 'Q (L/h) = 7.0' |
| CL covariate model `CL = theta1 * (CRCL / 60.0)` | -- | Table 3 footnote a; Table 4 footnote |
| V1 covariate model `V1 = theta2 * (WT / 49.5)` | -- | Table 3 footnote a; Table 4 footnote |
| `etalcl` | log(0.508^2 + 1) = 0.229577 | Table 4, omega(CL) 50.8% |
| `etalvc` | log(0.290^2 + 1) = 0.080750 | Table 4, omega(V1) 29.0% |
| No IIV on Q or V2 | -- | Basic Model ('did not improve model fitting') |
| `propSd` | 0.25 | Table 4, sigma = 0.25; error model `Cp = F*(1 + epsilon)` (Basic Model) |
| Covariate `CRCL` (raw Cockcroft-Gault, mL/min) | -- | Data Collection; Table 1 footnote a |
| Covariate `WT` (total body weight, kg) | -- | Data Collection; Table 3 footnote a |

# Typical-value check against Figure 2

Because the dose is given per kilogram and V1 is proportional to body weight,
the typical Cpeak per mg/kg barely depends on weight. Figure 2 brackets it
tightly. At 10 mg/kg nearly all patients reach Cpeak >= 16 but very few reach
32 mg/L (MIC 2 and 4). At 15 mg/kg nearly all reach 32 but none reach 64 mg/L
(MIC 4 and 8). At 20 mg/kg only 2.4% reach 64 mg/L, while at 25 mg/kg 80.4%
do. The median Cpeak per mg/kg must therefore lie between 64 / 25 = 2.56 and
64 / 20 = 3.2 mg/L.

```{r typical}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1, time = c(0, 1, 24), amt = c(49.5, 0, 0), rate = c(49.5 / 0.5, 0, 0),
  evid = c(1L, 0L, 0L), cmt = "central", WT = 49.5, CRCL = 60
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = typ_ev, returnType = "data.frame")
cpeak_per_mgkg <- typ$Cc[typ$time == 1]
cpeak_per_mgkg
cpeak_per_mgkg * c(10, 15, 20, 25, 30)
stopifnot(cpeak_per_mgkg >= 64 / 25, cpeak_per_mgkg < 64 / 20)
```

A typical patient (49.5 kg, CCr 60 mL/min) reaches
`r round(cpeak_per_mgkg, 2)` mg/L per mg/kg, inside the bracket.

# Virtual cohort

The paper resampled the observed covariate vectors, which are not published. A
200-subject cohort is drawn instead with body weight and creatinine clearance
from normal distributions matching the Table 1 mean and SD (50.4 +/- 10.4 kg;
60.3 +/- 33.9 mL/min), rejecting and redrawing values outside the observed
ranges (32.5-78 kg; 6.1-144 mL/min). The two are drawn independently because
their correlation is not reported. Between-subject random effects are drawn in
base R from the model's own `omega`, so the cohort is identical on every
rxode2 build, and they are passed to the typical-value model as data columns.

```{r cohort}
omega <- mod_ui$omega

draw_trunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rnorm(2 * n, mean, sd)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

set.seed(2017)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = draw_trunc_norm(n_sub, 50.4, 10.4, 32.5, 78),
  CRCL = draw_trunc_norm(n_sub, 60.3, 33.9, 6.1, 144),
  etalcl = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega["etalcl", "etalcl"])),
  etalvc = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega["etalvc", "etalvc"]))
)
summary(cohort[, c("WT", "CRCL")])
```

# Simulation

Each virtual patient receives a single 15 mg/kg dose (the regimen the paper
recommends) as a 0.5 h infusion, observed on a dense grid out to 72 h, from
which PKNCA extrapolates to infinity.

```{r simulate}
obs_times <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 30, 36,
               48, 60, 72)
dose_rows <- cohort |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = 15 * WT, rate = amt / 0.5, evid = 1L,
         cmt = "central")
obs_rows <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, rate, evid, cmt, WT, CRCL, etalcl, etalvc)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = events, returnType = "data.frame",
                       keep = c("WT", "CRCL"), atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10)
sim_obs <- sim |> filter(!is.na(Cc))
```

```{r profiles}
sim_obs |>
  mutate(crcl_band = cut(CRCL, c(0, 30, 60, 200),
                         labels = c("CRCL < 30", "CRCL 30-60", "CRCL > 60"))) |>
  group_by(crcl_band, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = crcl_band, fill = crcl_band)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 4, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after start of infusion (h)",
       y = "Amikacin serum concentration (mg/L)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Single 15 mg/kg dose over 0.5 h, 200 virtual patients",
       subtitle = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles by creatinine-clearance band; dashed line = 4 mg/L trough target") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no non-compartmental summary, so the NCA is checked against
the model's own identity: for linear IV kinetics with elimination only from the
central compartment, `AUC0-inf = Dose / CL` for each subject's individual
clearance.

Fast-clearing subjects fall to numerical-noise concentrations (including tiny
negative values) by 72 h. Concentrations below 1e-4 mg/L, far below the 0.8
mg/L assay limit, are set to zero before the NCA so that PKNCA treats them as
below the limit of quantification.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_obs |>
  mutate(treatment = "15 mg/kg single dose",
         Cc = ifelse(Cc < 1e-4, 0, Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  as.data.frame()
nca_dose <- dose_rows |>
  mutate(treatment = "15 mg/kg single dose") |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment) |>
  as.data.frame()

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                             doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                          intervals = intervals))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res), caption = "Simulated single-dose NCA (PKNCA).")

cl_typ <- exp(mod_ui$iniDf$est[mod_ui$iniDf$name == "lcl"])
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  mutate(id = as.integer(id)) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    cl_i = cl_typ * exp(etalcl) * CRCL / 60,
    auc_ref = 15 * WT / cl_i,
    pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES - auc_ref) / auc_ref
  )
summary(auc_chk$pct_diff)
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(auc_chk$pct_diff),
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

# Replicate Figure 2 and the trough target attainment

Figure 2 gives the probability of attaining Cpeak/MIC >= 8 for single doses of
10-30 mg/kg and MICs of 0.25-32 mg/L, with Cpeak the concentration 1 h after
the start of a 30 min infusion. The Results text quotes several of its values
(99.9% at MIC 4 and 0% at MIC 8 for 15 mg/kg, 2.4% at MIC 8 for 20 mg/kg, 80.4%
at MIC 8 for 25 mg/kg); the 10 mg/kg value at MIC 4 (about 2.5%) was read off
the figure by the maintainers. The text also gives the probability of a trough
below 4 mg/L for each dose; the trough is taken 24 h after the start of the
infusion (once-daily dosing).

```{r fig2-paper}
mics <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)
doses <- c(10, 15, 20, 25, 30)
paper_fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~mic, ~pta,
  10, 4, 2.5,
  10, 8, 0,
  15, 4, 99.9,
  15, 8, 0,
  20, 8, 2.4,
  20, 16, 0,
  25, 8, 80.4,
  25, 16, 0,
  30, 8, 100,
  30, 16, 0
)
# Every cell not listed above is 100% at a lower MIC or 0% at a higher MIC.
paper_fig2 <- tidyr::crossing(dose = doses, mic = mics) |>
  left_join(paper_fig2, by = c("dose", "mic")) |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  mutate(
    first_listed = min(mic[!is.na(pta)]),
    pta = dplyr::coalesce(pta, ifelse(mic < first_listed, 100, 0))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(dose, mic, pta)
paper_trough <- data.frame(dose = doses,
                           pta = c(86.6, 77.1, 67.9, 61.5, 54.5))
```

The same cohort is simulated two ways. The first carries the model's
between-subject variability on CL and V1. The second sets the random effects to
zero, so that only the resampled covariates (weight and creatinine clearance)
vary between patients. The model is linear, so one 1 mg/kg solve per patient is
scaled to every dose.

```{r fig2-sim}
pta_events <- bind_rows(
  cohort |> mutate(time = 0, amt = WT, rate = WT / 0.5, evid = 1L),
  cohort |> mutate(time = 1, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L),
  cohort |> mutate(time = 24, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

solve_unit <- function(ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    filter(time %in% c(1, 24)) |>
    select(id, time, Cc) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = Cc,
                       names_prefix = "c")
}
unit <- bind_rows(
  solve_unit(pta_events) |> mutate(reading = "with IIV"),
  solve_unit(mutate(pta_events, etalcl = 0, etalvc = 0)) |>
    mutate(reading = "covariates only")
)

sim_fig2 <- tidyr::crossing(unit, dose = doses, mic = mics) |>
  group_by(reading, dose, mic) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(c1 * dose / mic >= 8), .groups = "drop")
sim_trough <- tidyr::crossing(unit, dose = doses) |>
  group_by(reading, dose) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(c24 * dose < 4), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r fig2-plot}
bind_rows(
  sim_fig2,
  paper_fig2 |> mutate(reading = "Kato 2017 Figure 2")
) |>
  mutate(reading = factor(reading, c("Kato 2017 Figure 2", "covariates only",
                                     "with IIV"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(mic, pta, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~reading, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA, Cpeak/MIC >= 8 (%)",
       colour = "Dose (mg/kg)",
       title = "Replicates Figure 2 of Kato 2017") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r fig2-table}
fig2_cmp <- sim_fig2 |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = reading, values_from = pta) |>
  inner_join(paper_fig2 |> rename(paper = pta), by = c("dose", "mic")) |>
  filter(mic %in% c(4, 8, 16))
fig2_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
                "Paper (%)" = paper,
                "Simulated, covariates only (%)" = `covariates only`,
                "Simulated, with IIV (%)" = `with IIV`) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1,
               caption = "PTA for Cpeak/MIC >= 8 at the MICs where Figure 2 changes.")

trough_cmp <- sim_trough |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = reading, values_from = pta) |>
  inner_join(paper_trough |> rename(paper = pta), by = "dose")
trough_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Paper (%)" = paper,
                "Simulated, covariates only (%)" = `covariates only`,
                "Simulated, with IIV (%)" = `with IIV`) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Probability of a 24 h trough below 4 mg/L.")
```

The covariates-only simulation reproduces Figure 2: Cpeak/MIC >= 8 is reached
by nearly every patient up to the MIC at which the typical Cpeak falls below
8 x MIC, and by almost none above it, with the 25 mg/kg dose at MIC 8 near the
published 80.4%. Carrying the model's 29% IIV on V1 widens the Cpeak
distribution well beyond what Figure 2 shows (for example about 23% rather
than 2.4% at 20 mg/kg, MIC 8, and 56% rather than 80.4% at 25 mg/kg, MIC 8).
The trough target attainment points the same way: the covariates-only reading
reproduces the five quoted values to within about 4 percentage points, while
the reading with IIV falls 7-13 points below them. The published PTA therefore
appears to reflect covariate variability only; see Assumptions and deviations.
The trough attainment depends on the low-creatinine-clearance tail of the
cohort, which is drawn here from summary statistics rather than the paper's
own patients.

```{r fig2-gates}
fig2_all <- sim_fig2 |>
  inner_join(paper_fig2 |> rename(paper = pta), by = c("dose", "mic")) |>
  group_by(reading) |>
  summarise(mean_abs_diff = mean(abs(pta - paper)), .groups = "drop")
fig2_all
mad_cov <- fig2_all$mean_abs_diff[fig2_all$reading == "covariates only"]
mad_iiv <- fig2_all$mean_abs_diff[fig2_all$reading == "with IIV"]
cov_25_8 <- fig2_cmp$`covariates only`[fig2_cmp$dose == 25 & fig2_cmp$mic == 8]
trough_cov <- trough_cmp$`covariates only`
trough_iiv <- trough_cmp$`with IIV`

stopifnot(
  # Covariates-only reading matches the figure on average over all 40 cells.
  mad_cov < 3,
  # ... and clearly better than the reading with IIV.
  mad_iiv > 2 * mad_cov,
  # The one interior Figure 2 value quoted to a decimal.
  abs(cov_25_8 - 80.4) < 10,
  # Trough target attainment falls with dose and sits near the quoted values.
  all(diff(trough_cov) < 0),
  abs(median(trough_cov - paper_trough$pta)) < 5,
  # The reading with IIV sits further from the quoted trough values.
  median(abs(trough_iiv - paper_trough$pta)) >
    2 * median(abs(trough_cov - paper_trough$pta))
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error model.** Table 4 reports sigma = 0.25 with the unit ug/mL,
  but the Basic Model section states that the residual variability 'was
  modeled by a multiple error according to the equation Cp = F*(1 + epsilon)'.
  The printed equation is followed: `propSd = 0.25` (25%). Figure 1D supports
  this reading. Its individual weighted residuals stay within +/-2 at
  individual predictions up to about 65 mg/L, where observations deviate by up
  to about 20 mg/L. An additive SD of 0.25 mg/L would put those residuals near
  80. The figure's residual axes are themselves labelled in ug/mL, so the unit
  label in Table 4 is not taken as evidence of an additive model. The same
  section also says a combined error model was 'supposed', but only one sigma
  is reported.
* **IIV scale.** Table 4 reports omega(CL) = 50.8% and omega(V1) = 29.0%. They
  are read as coefficients of variation of log-normal random effects and
  converted with `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`. No correlation between the two
  random effects is reported, so they are independent.
* **V2 and Q.** The Table 4 footnote gives V2 = 7.72 L and Q = 7.0 L/h with no
  standard error or bootstrap summary, and no IIV. The paper does not say they
  were fixed, so they are encoded as ordinary (estimated) parameters.
* **Covariate reference values.** The printed equations normalize CCr by 60.0
  mL/min and weight by 49.5 kg, the Table 1 cohort medians. Both covariates
  enter linearly through the origin.
* **Published PTA appears to omit IIV.** The Methods say individual PK
  parameters were simulated 'from their estimated distribution in the final
  model with covariates'. Figure 2 and the quoted trough target attainment
  are nevertheless reproduced by a simulation in which only the covariates
  vary, and are not reproduced when the model's IIV is included. The packaged model carries the IIV as published; users
  replicating the paper's PTA should note this.
* **Virtual cohort.** The paper resampled 1000 observed covariate vectors that
  are not published. The cohort here is 200 subjects with weight and CCr drawn
  independently from truncated normal distributions matching Table 1, which is
  the expected source of the remaining differences in the trough target
  attainment.
* **Not reproduced.** The Figure 1 diagnostics need the individual data, which
  are not published. The cumulative fraction of response (Figure 3 and the
  quoted 76% at 15 mg/kg) needs the EUCAST *P. aeruginosa* MIC distribution the
  authors used, which is not given in the paper.
* **Covariate range.** The model was fitted to CCr of 6.1-144 mL/min and
  weight of 32.5-78 kg, from 1-2 samples per patient mostly within the first 3
  days of therapy. Clearance is proportional to CCr with no non-renal
  intercept, so it approaches zero as CCr approaches zero.
